newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 15.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 15.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - The main association of German advertising agencies, the GWA, says most of its members are satisfied with business in the first half of the year and predict further growth in the second half of 1997. "Seventy-eight percent of agencies reported a good-to-satisfying course of business for the first half of 1997, up from 76 percent last year," GWA president Lothar Leonhard says. (Reuter)
DUESSELDORF - A trend by British advertisers to use fast marketing -- a mixture of massive ad campaigns and sample distribution -- is headed toward Germany. (Handelsblatt)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

HAMBURG - Weekly news magazine Der Spiegel and Deutsche Bahn railway company say they have started a daily newspaper aimed at business readers on late-afternoon express trains. The newspaper begins with a weekly circulation of 30,000 and appears at 4 p.m. local time. The two companies say they plan to double the weekly circulation by October. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - A week after their much-hyped launch following a frantic subscription period, shares in television network ProSieben Media AG have settled at a solid but modest premium to their issue price. (Reuter)
HAMBURG - Italian fashion group Benetton is looking for a German publisher for its in-house-produced magazine Colors, marketing newsletter New Business reports. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BONN - The German government says it will delay taking any regulatory action against phone giant Deutsche Telekom until an appeal by the company is decided in the next few weeks in administrative court. The Post and Telecommunications Ministry on July 1 told Telekom it had until midnight July 14 to allow its rivals to gain access to its local telephone networks.
(Reuter)

MUNICH - Diversified utility Viag AG says it expects a rise in group sales in full-year 1997 and expects earnings to remain stable or rise slightly in the period. Viag's chemical unit SKW Trostberg and its aluminium unit VAW Aluminium AG perform particularly well in the first half of 1997, Viag says.
(Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

FRANKFURT - Roland Lock is new marketing director of brewery Henninger-Braeu AG. He was previously national key account manager at Kimberly-Clark. His predecessor at Henniger, Uwe Froesick, left of his own accord. (Horizont)

WALLDORF - Thomas Voigt is named editor-in-chief of business magazine "Impulse". He is currently editor-in-chief of ad industry publication Horizont and a member of the management team at publishing house Deutscher Fachverlag in Frankfurt.
(Kress)
WALLDORF - Michael Struck, sales director of private television station Sat1 in Frankfurt and Stuttgart, will soon become director of the company's sales management department. (Kress)

WALLDORF - TM3, a women's programming TV station, names its media product manager, Andrea Fleischhacker, sales director of its DRTV station as well. Susanne Kuenstler of sports channel DSF will also join the sales and marketing department as a product manager. Regine Kiefer is named new tm3 press editor.
(Kress)
